thread:
incident-bot: Pager — Canary divergence detected for deployment redwood-model/v3.2.1. Alert: tokenizer/weights mismatch + elevated 500s on canary pods. Dashboard: https://dash/redwood/alerts/1755123456 :rotating_light:
alex.k: I'm on it. Any clear customer impact yet?
maria.s: seeing ~2.3% error spike on canary-01 and canary-02. Samples show garbled tokens / decode errors (TOKENIZER_ERR). No elevated latencies.
chris_p: quick grep of artifacts: weightset tag = wset-20250308-v3.2.1, tokenizer reported in manifest = v2.8 but deployed tokenizer = v2.7. pipeline promoted wrong tokenizer alias.
alex.k: ok — proposed mitigation: 1) flip deploy feature flag to stop rollout, 2) drain canary traffic, 3) rollback to v3.2.0 if errors persist. Who can flip the flag?
oncall-liz: I can flip it now. Doing: `/ff toggle deploy-v3.2.1 off --reason "canary tokenizer mismatch"`
oncall-liz: /ff result: deploy-v3.2.1 -> OFF :white_check_mark: routing pauses for new activations.
infra-alerts: automated routing cutoff succeeded. No new canary allocations. Existing canary pods still serving until drained.
maria.s: running quick health checks and grabbing more samples. Running: ```rctl check --service redwood-model --targets canary-01,canary-02 --level brief```
maria.s: sample bad output: "Hello, � token sequence" — consistent with tokenizer/decoder mismatch.
chris_p: I started a rebuild to repack weights + tokenizer pinned to v2.8. New artifact tag: wset-20250308-v3.2.1-fixed (building now). ETA ~18m.
alex.k: while build completes, let's prepare rollback path. Maria, can you trigger a controlled rollback if errors don't drop below baseline in 10m?
maria.s: yes. Command we'll run: ```rctl rollback --service redwood-model --to v3.2.0 --force && kubectl rollout restart deploy/redwood-model-canary -n prod```
oncall-liz: initiating traffic drain now. Monitoring metrics in realtime. If errors persist after drain + 5m stabilization, I'll execute rollback.
sre-team: watching infra metrics. Not seeing wider rollout; containment looks good. We'll stand by for rollback.
support-bot: notifying support: "Potential small percentage of requests to canary may have garbled output. No auth/data leak observed. Triage in progress"
alex.k: Chris — once fixed artifact is ready, we want an explicit manifest-hash check before redeploy. Maria, add a preflight check step.
chris_p: will add a manifest comparator and CI gate. I'll also stamp artifact with tokenizer_hash and weight_hash; we will not allow promo unless both match.
maria.s: rollback executed at 1755123530: `rctl rollback ...` and `kubectl rollout restart ...` — canary pods now on v3.2.0. Error rate back to baseline within 90s.
oncall-liz: rollback complete. Monitoring shows errors dropped to normal. Flipped feature flag remains off.
alex.k: great. Impact summary for ops: small % of canary traffic affected; no customer data exposure; mitigation: FF off, drain, rollback. Next steps: postmortem + release pipeline hardening.
chris_p: build completed and artifact uploaded to staging with correct tokenizer v2.8. Will coordinate a canary redeploy after CI manifest checks pass and SRE signoff.
maria.s: quick note for follow-up: root cause = deploy pipeline allowed floating tokenizer alias; release script didn't validate tokenizer hash against model manifest. Proposed fixes: manifest-hash preflight, stricter artifact pinning, and longer canary observation window (30m).
alex.k: adding action items and assigning owners. I'll file a postmortem and link here. Thanks everyone — closing pager. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Pager resolved — incident auto-ack closed at 1755123580. Postmortem link will be posted to #postmortems when ready.
